No Android permissions requested, including no INTERNET permission.

New behavior:
Limited legacy NCP compatibility adaptation, with user-reviewed choices and final confirmation.
Canonical 638-byte NCP0100, supported color bases, numeric old settings and a 578-byte custom curve only.
Unknown records/versions/metadata/sentinels, Auto and monochrome are rejected before USB opens.
The original curve bytes are preserved without an endian swap.
Middle-range sharpening and clarity are user choices; UI defaults to 1 and 0 respectively.
Individual sharpening/quick=0 and curve-mode contrast=0/brightness=0 are explicitly displayed adaptation values.
These values are not claimed to match Nikon firmware's legacy-import completion rules.
Preview freezes original bytes, checksum, target and choices; backend independently reconverts those same inputs.
The same fresh-nine-slot, twice-observed-empty target, single registration, exact readback and cleanup guards apply.
The NCP registration entry point accepts original NCP plus explicit choices; it does not accept arbitrary wire data.
Copy behavior remains source-verified and is never labeled as an NCP registration.
Metadata and choices survive converter, USB/PTP, readback and cleanup errors.
ncpRegistrationVerified means adapted payload registration and exact readback plus confirmed cleanup.
ncpImportVerified, conversionEquivalentToNative and photoEffectVerified remain false.
No automatic retry, rollback, deletion, preset selection or mode-change request.
Double empty observations are not an atomic camera guard; avoid editing slots from another actor during import.
